parts.desc: An eight-spoked oak wheel on the foot of the tail. Turning it winds the chain to a kruipaal and pulls the cap, sails and tail round into the wind (photo 09).

parts.name: Winding posts (kruipalen)
parts.desc: A ring of oak posts round the mill: the winding chain is hooked to the post in the right direction and the kruirad pulls the cap round to it.

parts.name: Burned stump (1921-1929)
parts.desc: On New Year's Eve 1921 the mill caught fire 'because it had run too hard that day'. Thatch, cap, sails and floors burned; the brick base and charred stubs of the corner posts were left, with the iron windshaft lying where it fell.

parts.name: Youth hostel 'Weideheuvel' (1929-1990)
parts.desc: In 1929 J.H. van Twisk opened the first youth hostel of the Netherlands in the stump: a white-boarded octagonal storey with windows all round on the old brick base, under a thatched octagonal roof. The form is reconstructed (no plan found).

parts.name: House on the mill base (today)
parts.desc: Today Binnenweg 22 is a house built on the octagonal brick base: a steep octagonal slate-grey roof with dormers and roof lights, and a flat-roofed brick wing (photo 31).

parts.name: Alder carr, osier and reed on the Amstel levee
parts.desc: Before reclamation the clay levee of the Amstel carries a wet alder wood (alder carr, Alnus glutinosa 12-20 m) with grey willow and osier thickets, and a belt of common reed (Phragmites, 2-3 m) at the water's edge. Overbank clay made the levee the most fertile strip of the peatland.
facts: Peat succession: open water -> reed -> sedge -> alder/birch carr -> Sphagnum raised bog (de Bont 2015; Ettema 2005).

parts.name: Birch fen
parts.desc: Between 50 and 300 m from the river the ground is sedge and reed fen with downy birch (Betula pubescens, 8-15 m) and scattered alder: the zone where the raised bog grades into the river levee.

parts.name: Open raised bog
parts.desc: Beyond about 300 m from the river lies open raised bog: Sphagnum lawns in rust, ochre and green, heather (Calluna, Erica tetralix) and cotton grass tussocks, bog pools and a few stunted birch and Scots pine 2-5 m tall. The surface rises gently eastward, about 1-2 m per kilometre.

parts.name: Alder and willow left on the river strip (dike)
parts.desc: The colonists clear most of the carr, but alders and willows survive on the river strip and along the bank: firewood, wattle rods and shade for cattle.

parts.name: Alder and willow left on the river strip (meadow)
parts.desc: The colonists clear most of the carr, but alders and willows survive on the river strip and along the bank: firewood, wattle rods and shade for cattle.

parts.name: Elder and hawthorn hedges on the kades (meadow)
parts.desc: Low dams (kades) along the back and side ditches keep water from the higher, still unreclaimed peat out of each cope plot; elder and hawthorn hedges grow on them.

parts.name: Arable strips: barley, oats and flax
parts.desc: In the first two centuries the drained peat is still high and dry enough for grain: barley, oats and flax on the higher eastern ends of the cope plots, hay and pasture nearer the river. Rye was not grown (too wet in winter). By about 1350-1500 the land has sunk too far and dairy takes over.
facts: Excavated 11th-12th c. peat farms (Assendelft) yielded emmer, barley, oats and flax, no rye (Ettema 2005).

parts.name: Pollard willows along the ditches (meadow)
parts.desc: Pollard willows (knotwilgen) line the ditches: their crowns are cut back every 3-5 years for rods, stakes and firewood, and their roots hold the soft peat banks.
facts: The giant pollard willow in Rembrandt's 'The Omval' (1645), 3.3 km north, is the model for these trees.
Half the trees are drawn freshly cut (short shoots), half grown out: the 3-5 year cutting cycle shown side by side.

parts.name: Pollard willows along the ditches (meadow)
parts.desc: Pollard willows (knotwilgen) line the ditches: their crowns are cut back every 3-5 years for rods, stakes and firewood, and their roots hold the soft peat banks.
facts: The giant pollard willow in Rembrandt's 'The Omval' (1645), 3.3 km north, is the model for these trees.
Half the trees are drawn freshly cut (short shoots), half grown out: the 3-5 year cutting cycle shown side by side.

parts.name: Reed fringe along the Amstel
parts.desc: Common reed (Phragmites australis) grows in a narrow fringe where the Amstel bank meets the water; it was cut in winter for thatch.

parts.name: Reed along the main drains
parts.desc: Reed belts along the wider main drains (tochten) that carry the polder water to the mill.

parts.name: Elm and ash rows on the dike road (dike)
parts.desc: Rows of elm and ash line the Binnenweg on its dike, as in the c.1900 photograph of the Amstel dike at Ouderkerk (hay wagon under tall elms). Elms were planted for timber and shade on dike roads from the 17th century; they were lost to Dutch elm disease after 1920.

parts.name: Tree-lined dike road (20th century) (dike)
parts.desc: Ash and Canadian poplar along the river side of the Binnenweg: the tree-lined road of the 1958 photographs, with a pile revetment at the water. Some still stand today north of the house.

parts.name: Trees on the west-bank Amsteldijk (dike)
parts.desc: In 1656 the Amsteldijk on the far (west) bank was widened to 11 m and tree planting along its footpath was allowed 'to beautify the Amsteldijk'; the towpath ran beside them.

parts.name: Yard trees before 1900 (yard)
parts.desc: Bushy yard trees round the farmhouse as in Rembrandt's farm etchings (B219, B228): pollard willows, ash and elm for shelter from the wind and for timber.

parts.name: Yard trees before 1900 (meadow)
parts.desc: Bushy yard trees round the farmhouse as in Rembrandt's farm etchings (B219, B228): pollard willows, ash and elm for shelter from the wind and for timber.

parts.name: Tall trees by the house (yard)
parts.desc: Tall ash, white willow and Canadian poplar (15-22 m) stand north and south of the house on the 1958 photographs and in today's 3D aerial view; they frame the voorhuis from the river.

parts.name: Tall trees by the house (dike)
parts.desc: Tall ash, white willow and Canadian poplar (15-22 m) stand north and south of the house on the 1958 photographs and in today's 3D aerial view; they frame the voorhuis from the river.

parts.name: Tall trees by the house (meadow)
parts.desc: Tall ash, white willow and Canadian poplar (15-22 m) stand north and south of the house on the 1958 photographs and in today's 3D aerial view; they frame the voorhuis from the river.

parts.name: Orchard (meadow)
parts.desc: A small orchard of apple and pear trees beside the farm, for the household and the market boats to Amsterdam.

parts.name: Beech hedge in front of the voorhuis
parts.desc: A clipped beech hedge about 1.2 m high runs between the Binnenweg and the 1894 front, screening the cellar windows (photograph 2022). Beech keeps its brown leaves through winter.

parts.name: Binnenweg: cart track on the river kade
parts.desc: A rutted clay cart track along the top of the river kade, the first road of the colonists. The kade became necessary once the reclaimed land sank below the river.

parts.name: Binnenweg: clay and shell road
parts.desc: The Binnenweg as a packed clay road dressed with crushed shell, about 3-4 m wide, as on the c.1900 photograph of the Amstel dike at Ouderkerk.

parts.name: Binnenweg: gravel road
parts.desc: A fine-chipping gravel surface (the 1958 photographs show a loose chip road with grass verges).

parts.name: Binnenweg: asphalt road with dashed edge lines
parts.desc: Today's narrow asphalt Binnenweg, about 3.5-4 m wide with dashed white edge lines (photograph 2022). Cyclists, walkers and farm traffic only.

parts.name: West-bank towpath (jaagpad)
parts.desc: The towpath of the Amsterdam-Ouderkerk trekschuit service ran on the far, west bank (Amsteldijk): a sand and shell path by the water along which a horse towed the passenger barge on a long line. Rolpalen, posts with vertical wooden rollers, kept the line off the bank at bends.
facts: Trekschuit Amsterdam-Uithoorn along the Amstel from 1599 (ONH).
About 150 rolpalen stood along the west side of the Amstel (ONH 'Rolpalen langs de Amstel').

parts.name: Wooden flap culvert (klepduiker)
parts.desc: A plank box culvert through the river kade with a hinged flap (klep) on the river end: at low river water the polder water pushes the flap open and drains out by gravity; at high water the river presses it shut. It was the only drainage before the windmills of 1637.
facts: Before the mills, polders drained through sluices and heulen at low river water (site research §3).

parts.name: Farm bridges over the field ditches
parts.desc: Plank bridges (kavelbruggen) on timber piles carry cattle and hay carts over the parcel ditches; their rails are painted white so they show at dusk, as in Rembrandt's 'Six's Bridge' (1645).

parts.name: Farm bridges over the field ditches (concrete)
parts.desc: After about 1950 the farm bridges are rebuilt as concrete slabs on concrete abutments with steel or timber rails.

parts.name: Earth dams with culverts and field gates
parts.desc: Where a parcel needed a fixed crossing the ditch was closed with an earth dam (dam) with a culvert pipe through it, so the water still flowed. A timber field gate (hek) with a diagonal brace closed the dam to cattle. Gates were painted white.

specs.Culvert: timber box, later concrete pipe Ø 0.6 m

parts.name: Inlet sluice with stop logs
parts.desc: In dry summers the polder let Amstel water in to keep the ditches wet (as stock fence and for the cattle) through a small inlet sluice in the dike: a timber head with grooves in which horizontal stop logs (schotbalken) are stacked to hold the river back.

parts.name: Timber pile bank revetment (beschoeiing)
parts.desc: A close row of round timber piles with a horizontal waling holds the dike toe against the wash of boats and waves, as on the 1958 photograph of the Amstel in front of the farm.

specs.Piles: Ø ≈0.2 m, tops ≈0.1 m above the water
specs.Line: ≈140 m in front of the farm

parts.name: Cattle drinking places
parts.desc: Where a parcel had no pump, cattle drank from the ditch at a drinking place: a short, gently sloped notch in the bank, fenced by a pair of rails so the animals could not walk into the ditch.

parts.name: Ouderkerk church, tower with needle spire
parts.desc: Ouderkerk's medieval church at the Amstel-Bullewijk confluence (first church c. 1000, stone church c. 1100) with a square tower and a tall needle spire, the landmark on the southern horizon in the 1608 and 1670 prints and in Rembrandt's etchings. The spire was destroyed in the storm of 1 August 1674.
facts: Rembrandt's 'Six's Bridge' (1645) shows this tower on the left horizon.

parts.name: Ouderkerk church tower stump after the storm of 1 Aug 1674
parts.desc: After lightning and the storm of 1 August 1674 (the same storm wrecked the nave of Utrecht cathedral) the Ouderkerk spire is gone and the church stands as a roofless ruin with a tower stump for a century.

parts.name: Amstelkerk (J.E. de Witte), low church with lantern
parts.desc: The Amstelkerk of 1775 by J.E. de Witte replaced the ruined church: a low neoclassical cross-shaped church with hipped roofs and a small open lantern on the crossing, white-plastered (Jacob Olie 1897).

parts.name: Sint-Urbanuskerk Ouderkerk (Cuypers), spire
parts.desc: Cuypers' neo-Gothic Sint-Urbanuskerk (1867) with a west tower and a slender spire just over 50 m: from 1867 the tallest point on the southern horizon (photograph ANWZ00489, c.1900).

parts.name: Sint-Urbanuskerk Duivendrecht
parts.desc: The Catholic Sint-Urbanuskerk of Duivendrecht (1878) on the ENE horizon beyond the railway.

parts.name: Molen De Zwaan (Klein-Duivendrechtse polder)
parts.desc: Molen De Zwaan (1638), the thatched octagonal drainage mill of the Klein-Duivendrechtse polder, 1.24 km south on the Binnenweg. It is not the farm's own mill (that is Strandvliet, 511 m NE); it stopped work in 1909 when a steam station took over, and still stands.

parts.name: Riekermolen (moved here 1961)
parts.desc: The Riekermolen, a 1636 polder mill moved in 1961 to the Amsteldijk at the Kalfjeslaan, with a statue of Rembrandt beside it.

parts.name: West-bank Middelpolder mill
parts.desc: The drainage mill of the Middelpolder across the Amstel at the mouth of the Machinetocht ("Middelpolder Waterm." on the 1850 map), replaced by a motor pumping station by 1955.
facts: Start date unknown: the mill is on the 1850 map; 1640 is an estimate for the first polder mill.

parts.name: West-bank motor pumping station
parts.desc: A low brick motor pumping station ('Motorgem.' on the 1955 map) replaces the Middelpolder mill.

parts.name: Amsterdam Oude Kerk tower
parts.desc: Amsterdam Oude Kerk tower on the northern skyline, 6.7 km away: only a faint grey needle about half a degree above the horizon on clear days.

parts.name: Amsterdam Zuiderkerk tower
parts.desc: Amsterdam Zuiderkerk tower on the northern skyline, 6.2 km away: only a faint grey needle about half a degree above the horizon on clear days.

parts.name: Amsterdam Westertoren
parts.desc: Amsterdam Westertoren on the northern skyline, 6.8 km away: only a faint grey needle about half a degree above the horizon on clear days.

parts.name: Amsterdam-Utrecht railway embankment
parts.desc: The Amsterdam-Utrecht railway (Rhijnspoor), opened 18 December 1843, on a low embankment 2.2 km east through Duivendrecht: the first line to cut the polder. Steam-train smoke drifts along the eastern horizon until electrification.

parts.name: Railway catenary masts
parts.desc: Electrification in 1938 (1.5 kV DC) adds lines of catenary masts with portal booms: a fine comb of uprights along the eastern horizon.

parts.name: A2 motorway (one carriageway)
parts.desc: The A2 opens its first carriageway Ouderkerk-Vinkeveen on 21 October 1952, on a low sand embankment 810 m north-east of the farm.

parts.name: A2 motorway
parts.desc: From 1 April 1954 the full dual carriageway Amsterdam-Utrecht: a low embankment with a steady band of traffic, the main sound of the polder today.

parts.name: Bijlmermeer high-rise slabs
parts.desc: The Bijlmermeer: from 1966 (first pile 13 Dec 1966, first residents 1968) a honeycomb of bent ten-storey slabs 3-4 km east-south-east, a grey wall on the horizon by 1975.

parts.name: Johan Cruijff ArenA
parts.desc: The Johan Cruijff ArenA (1996), due east 2.4 km: a white oval stadium with a retractable arched roof, the centre of today's eastern skyline in both reference aerials.

parts.name: Rembrandt Tower
parts.desc: The Rembrandt Tower (1994) at the Omval, 3.4 km north, 135 m: the tallest building of Amsterdam, a slim glass tower with a pointed crown.

parts.name: Amstel III and ArenA-district towers
parts.desc: Office and hotel towers of Amstel III and the ArenA boulevard (1990s-2020s), 60-120 m, cluster around the stadium on the eastern horizon.

parts.name: De Drie Fonteinen (Binnenweg 16)
parts.desc: The neighbouring farm 'De Drie Fonteinen' about 100 m south, built in 1810 after its predecessor 'Na Druk Geluk' burnt in 1809.

parts.name: Farm 'Na Druk Geluk' (predecessor)
parts.desc: The farm on the De Drie Fonteinen site before the fire of 1809 (form EST: an Amstelland hallehuis).

parts.name: Strandvliet farm
parts.desc: The Strandvliet farm group about 250 m north, by the private ferry ('Pont (particuliere)') on the 1900 map.

parts.name: West-bank houses
parts.desc: Scattered dike houses and small farms along the Amsteldijk on the Amstelveen side (1832 map).

parts.name: West-bank houses (20th c.)
parts.desc: From the 1920s the Amsteldijk on the west bank fills up with houses and allotment sheds.

parts.name: Ouderkerk village roofs
parts.desc: The roofs of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel round its church at the Amstel-Bullewijk confluence, 2 km south.

parts.name: Distant tree belts
parts.desc: Trees round the villages, farms, dike roads and country estates on the horizon; in the 20th century also the Amsterdamse Bos, parks and the green belts of Amstelveen and Zuidoost.

parts.name: Distant tree belts (20th c.)
parts.desc: Trees round the villages, farms, dike roads and country estates on the horizon; in the 20th century also the Amsterdamse Bos, parks and the green belts of Amstelveen and Zuidoost.

parts.name: Amstel channel clay
parts.desc: Under the river bed lie the fine grey clays and silts the slow Amstel carried and dropped in its channel between about 1000 BC and AD 1122 (de Gans 2015).

parts.name: Storm clay of 1164 / 1170 on the levee
parts.desc: The storm surges of 1164 and 1170 laid a clay cap on the Amstel banks. It is why the river strip with the dike and the Binnenweg stands higher than the meadow behind it: clay hardly shrinks, peat does.

parts.name: Made ground of the farm terrace
parts.desc: The farm stands on a terrace of dumped clay, dung, ash and rubble, raised again and again as the land sank (the S1 house mound was topped up every decade). Brick fragments and potsherds speckle it.

parts.name: Hollandveen peat
parts.desc: Five to six metres of Holland peat: reed and sedge peat at the base, wood peat, then Sphagnum bog peat on top. Drained since about 1100, it shrinks and oxidises: the meadow has gone down about 3.5 m (ground level +1.5 m NAP around AD 1000, -2.1 m today). Scrub the years to watch it sink.
facts: Erkens et al. 2016: about 1.9 m average drainage subsidence of the coastal peat over 1000 years.

parts.name: Basal peat and older marine clay
parts.desc: Below the Holland peat: thin basal peat and the marine clays of the Calais / Wormer deposits laid down by the sea before the coastal barrier closed. They hardly compact any more.

parts.name: Pleistocene sand
parts.desc: The firm Pleistocene sand at about 12 m below NAP: the layer the piles of Amsterdam are driven into.

parts.name: Lost peat (oxidised since reclamation)
parts.desc: The translucent block shows the peat that has disappeared since the reclamation: about 3.5 m of meadow, less on the clay-capped dike. It was not washed away but shrank as it dried and oxidised to CO2.

specs.Lost: ≈3.6 m in the meadow, ≈1.3 m on the dike

parts.name: Water level: Amstel −0.40 m NAP
parts.desc: The Amstel boezem level, managed at −0.40 m NAP since the dam in Amsterdam (1265-75).

parts.name: Water level: polder ditches −2.45 m NAP
parts.desc: The polder water level, kept 0.3-0.5 m below the meadow by pumping (−2.45 m NAP today).

parts.name: NAP gauge staff (peilschaal)
parts.desc: A painted gauge board on an oak post at the river bank in front of the farm, marked in decimetres relative to NAP (Amsterdam Ordnance Datum). It stays fixed while the years move the water and the land: read off the Amstel at −0.40 and compare the meadow behind the dike, +1.5 m around AD 1000, −1.6 in 1910, −2.1 m today.
facts: NAP zero is the average summer high tide of the IJ at Amsterdam in 1683-84.

parts.name: Log boat: hollowed oak trunk
parts.desc: A single oak trunk hollowed with fire and adze, 8.6 m long and about a metre wide, with two transverse ribs left standing to stiffen it and solid ends (the type found at Nigtevecht on the Vecht, 10th-9th c. BC). People of the wild-peat era came up the Amstel in such boats to fish and hunt.
facts: Dimensions from the Nigtevecht log boat (10th-9th c. BC) [REF machines_boats §3].

parts.name: Log boat: paddles
parts.desc: Leaf-bladed ash paddles [EST: the Nigtevecht find has no paddles; Bronze Age paddles from NW Europe are leaf-shaped].

parts.name: Punter: bottom planking
parts.desc: The flat bottom (bodemplanken): heavy planks laid edge to edge along the boat, rising at the ends where the bottom sweeps up into the stems.

parts.name: Punter: side planking
parts.desc: Three overlapping (clinker, overnaads) oak strakes, oiled; the bottom is tarred. Hard chine, flared sides.

parts.name: Punter: stems
parts.desc: Stem and sternpost (voor- en achtersteven): the end timbers the planks are nailed into.

parts.name: Punter: frames
parts.desc: Frames (spanten: floors and futtocks) that hold the planking in shape.

parts.name: Punter: thwarts
parts.desc: Thwarts (doften) across the boat.

parts.name: Punter: quant pole
parts.desc: The quant pole (boom, 4-5 m, ash) with a forked foot that does not sink into the soft peat bottom: the punter is pushed along by walking it from bow to stern.

parts.name: Punter: reed sheaves
parts.desc: A load of reed sheaves (riet) cut in the polder [EST: punters carried peat, hay, reed, dung and cattle feed].

parts.name: Hooipraam: bottom planking
parts.desc: The flat bottom (bodemplanken): heavy planks laid edge to edge along the boat, rising at the ends where the bottom sweeps up into the stems.

parts.name: Hooipraam: side planking
parts.desc: Tarred clinker sides; the bottom curves up at both ends into wide flat 'praam' ends.

parts.name: Hooipraam: frames
parts.desc: Frames (spanten: floors and futtocks) that hold the planking in shape.

parts.name: Hooipraam: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: The berghout: a heavy rubbing strake along each side that takes the knocks at quays, locks and other boats.

parts.name: Hooipraam: end boards
parts.desc: The square end boards (koppen) that close the praam's sloping ends.

parts.name: Hooipraam: hay load
parts.desc: A load of loose hay stacked high over the hold, brought from the outlying meadows to the farm's hay barrack.

parts.name: Hooipraam: lashings and pole
parts.desc: Lashings over the hay and the punting pole.

parts.name: Trekschuit: bottom planking
parts.desc: The flat bottom (bodemplanken): heavy planks laid edge to edge along the boat, rising at the ends where the bottom sweeps up into the stems.

parts.name: Trekschuit: side planking
parts.desc: Five overlapping oak strakes painted dark green above a tarred bottom [EST colours]. Ordinance size 54 × 9¼ Amsterdam feet = 15.29 × 2.62 m [REF].

parts.name: Trekschuit: stems
parts.desc: Stem and sternpost (voor- en achtersteven): the end timbers the planks are nailed into.

parts.name: Trekschuit: frames
parts.desc: Frames (spanten: floors and futtocks) that hold the planking in shape.

parts.name: Trekschuit: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: The berghout: a heavy rubbing strake along each side that takes the knocks at quays, locks and other boats.

parts.name: Trekschuit: decks
parts.desc: Planked foredeck where the towing mast stands, and the small after deck where the skipper steers.

parts.name: Trekschuit: ruim (passenger hold) and tent
parts.desc: The ruim: the open passenger hold for 24-30 people on benches along the sides, under a canvas tent stretched over wooden hoops [REF machines_boats §3].

parts.name: Trekschuit: roef (first-class cabin)
parts.desc: The roef: a low cabin aft for the eight first-class passengers, painted red with white window frames [EST colours; REF 8 seats].

parts.name: Trekschuit: towing mast
parts.desc: The short towing mast (jaagmast) stepped on the foredeck. The towline is made fast to a ring part-way up so it clears the reeds and the rolpalen guide it round the bends.

parts.name: Trekschuit: rudder
parts.desc: A barn-door rudder hung on the sternpost with iron pintles and gudgeons.

parts.name: Trekschuit: tiller
parts.desc: The curved tiller (helmstok), reaching over the after deck.

parts.name: Trekschuit: towline (jaaglijn)
parts.desc: The jaaglijn: a 1 cm hemp line about 70 m long from the towing mast to the swingletree behind the horse on the west-bank towpath. At the bends it ran round rolpalen, posts with vertical rollers.

parts.name: Tjalk: bottom planking
parts.desc: The flat bottom (bodemplanken): heavy planks laid edge to edge along the boat, rising at the ends where the bottom sweeps up into the stems.

parts.name: Tjalk: side planking
parts.desc: Carvel (gladboord) oak planking, tarred; round bow and stern, flat bottom, strongly rising sheer. Wooden until c.1900, then riveted iron [REF].

parts.name: Tjalk: stems
parts.desc: Stem and sternpost (voor- en achtersteven): the end timbers the planks are nailed into.

parts.name: Tjalk: frames
parts.desc: Frames (spanten: floors and futtocks) that hold the planking in shape.

parts.name: Tjalk: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: The berghout: a heavy rubbing strake along each side that takes the knocks at quays, locks and other boats.

parts.name: Tjalk: decks, hatches and gunwale
parts.desc: Fore and after decks, narrow side decks, the hold under curved hatch boards (luiken) on a coaming, and the varnished gunwale rail.

parts.name: Tjalk: roef (skipper's cabin)
parts.desc: The roef aft: the skipper's family lived here in one small cabin.

parts.name: Tjalk: mast and tabernacle
parts.desc: A pine mast about 14 m above deck [EST] stepped in a tabernacle (mastkoker) so it can be lowered to pass bridges, with a wind vane (vlögel) at the truck.

parts.name: Tjalk: leeboards
parts.desc: Two pear-shaped varnished oak leeboards (zwaarden), one each side. The lee one is lowered to stop the flat-bottomed barge drifting sideways; the windward one is hauled up.

parts.name: Tjalk: leeboard pivots
parts.desc: Iron pivot bolts (zwaardbouten) on which the leeboards swing.

parts.name: Tjalk: rudder
parts.desc: The large outboard rudder (roer) hung on the sternpost, wide at the foot.

parts.name: Tjalk: tiller
parts.desc: The swan-necked tiller (helmstok) over the after deck.

parts.name: Tjalk: boom and gaff
parts.desc: The long boom (giek) and the short curved gaff (gaffel) typical of Dutch flat-bottomed sailing barges.

parts.name: Tjalk: tan-bark sails
parts.desc: Gaff mainsail and jib of cotton/flax canvas dressed with tan-bark (oak bark and fat) against rot, which gives the red-brown colour.

parts.name: Tjalk: rigging
parts.desc: Forestay (voorstag), shrouds (want) to the gunwale each side, peak halyard and mainsheet.

parts.name: Steamboat: bottom plating
parts.desc: Riveted iron bottom plates with a red-lead anti-fouling below the waterline [EST].

parts.name: Steamboat: hull plating
parts.desc: Riveted iron side plating, black, with a fine plumb bow and an overhanging counter stern sheltering the propeller [EST, after the c.1900 Amstel postcard].

parts.name: Steamboat: frames
parts.desc: Angle-iron frames every 0.5 m.

parts.name: Steamboat: deck
parts.desc: Laid pine deck.

parts.name: Steamboat: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: Timber rubbing strakes with an iron half-round.

parts.name: Steamboat: railings
parts.desc: White painted railings round the passenger deck.

parts.name: Steamboat: awning
parts.desc: A canvas awning on iron stanchions over the passenger deck: the c.1900 postcard shows the whole deck under a flat canopy with a scalloped valance [PHOTO 20].

parts.name: Steamboat: engine casing
parts.desc: White deckhouse over the boiler and engine, with skylights.

parts.name: Steamboat: vertical boiler
parts.desc: A vertical fire-tube boiler [EST] fired with coal; steam at about 7-8 atm for the engine.

parts.name: Steamboat: compound engine
parts.desc: An inverted vertical compound engine [EST]: high- and low-pressure cylinders on columns driving the crankshaft and a small flywheel.

parts.name: Steamboat: propeller shaft
parts.desc: The propeller shaft through the stern tube.

parts.name: Steamboat: propeller
parts.desc: Four-bladed bronze screw, about 0.9 m across [EST].

parts.name: Steamboat: rudder
parts.desc: Balanced iron rudder under the counter.

parts.name: Steamboat: funnel
parts.desc: A tall thin funnel through the awning, buff with a black top [EST].

parts.name: Steamboat: benches and wheel
parts.desc: Slatted benches for the passengers and the steering wheel forward.

parts.name: Milk praam: riveted iron hull
parts.desc: A small riveted iron praam with raked ends (dekschuit type) that collected milk churns from the farm landings for the dairy factory [REF/EST].

parts.name: Milk praam: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: Timber rubbing strakes.

parts.name: Milk praam: hold floor and gangboards
parts.desc: Hold floor (buikdenning) and side gangboards for poling.

parts.name: Milk praam: milk churns
parts.desc: Galvanised 40-litre milk churns (melkbussen), collected every morning.

parts.name: Milk praam: motor
parts.desc: A single-cylinder hot-bulb or petrol engine under a casing, with its exhaust pipe [EST].

parts.name: Milk praam: rudder and tiller
parts.desc: Rudder and tiller.

parts.name: Coal barge: hull
parts.desc: An iron praam, deep-laden with coal for the steam gemaal's boilers.

parts.name: Coal barge: rubbing strakes
parts.desc: Rubbing strakes.

parts.name: Coal barge: coal
parts.desc: Steam coal for the gemaal's Cornish boiler [EST].

parts.name: Coal barge: rudder and tiller
parts.desc: Rudder and tiller.

parts.name: Rowing eight: cedar shell (1933-1980)
parts.desc: A wooden racing eight: a cedar-skinned shell on light frames, the type raced in the first Head of the River Amstel (1933, 8 km Ouderkerk -> Amsterdam).

parts.name: Rowing eight: composite shell (1980-)
parts.desc: A modern carbon/composite racing eight.

parts.name: Rowing eight: sliding seats and stretchers
parts.desc: Eight sliding seats on rails, the foot-stretchers and the coxswain's seat in the stern.

parts.name: Rowing eight: riggers
parts.desc: Alternating outriggers carrying the swivels (gates) 0.83 m out from the centreline: sweep rowing, one oar per rower.

parts.name: Rowing eight: oars
parts.desc: Eight sweep oars (≈3.8 m) with cleaver blades, resting flat on the water (easy-all) [EST].

parts.name: Salonboat: steel hull
parts.desc: A low steel hull, navy blue, built to pass under Amsterdam's bridges.

parts.name: Salonboat: rubber fender
parts.desc: Black rubber fender all round.

parts.name: Salonboat: deck
parts.desc: Teak-laid deck.

parts.name: Salonboat: saloon
parts.desc: The glazed saloon with a white roof [EST].

parts.name: Electric shuttle: hull
parts.desc: A round-bilged sloep-type hull, glossy blue [PHOTO oa_boat_amstel], carrying guests between Ouderkerk and the farm's jetty since 2023.

parts.name: Electric shuttle: rope fender
parts.desc: A thick rope fender round the gunwale and hanging blue fenders.

parts.name: Electric shuttle: floor and benches
parts.desc: Teak floor and benches along the sides.

parts.name: Electric shuttle: canopy
parts.desc: White canvas canopy with clear roll-up windows on a stainless frame [PHOTO oa_boat_amstel].

parts.name: Electric shuttle: electric pod drive
parts.desc: Electric pod motor and propeller under the stern [EST].

parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (8 slots).

parts.name: Stalled cow smalls 1325-1450
parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (10 slots).

parts.name: Stalled cows 1450-1575
parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (10 slots).

parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (1 slots).

parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (20 slots).

parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (1 slots).

parts.name: Stalled cows 1889-2013
parts.desc: Animals standing or lying in the stall places of the house (20 slots).

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 1175-1575
parts.desc: Small medieval cattle (1.08-1.15 m at the withers), mixed brown and red: 6-8 head in S1, only 4-6 per farm in 1514 [REF Gouda-Oostpolder; Informacie 1514].

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 1575-1750
parts.desc: 18-25 cattle per farm in the later 17th c.; herds still mixed, about 2/3 red(-pied) and 1/3 black(-pied) [REF Bieleman].

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 1750-1850
parts.desc: After c.1750 black and black-pied cattle dominate in the west; rinderpest waves cut herds in the 18th c. [REF Bieleman].

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 1850-1970
parts.desc: Fries-Hollands black-pied cows: about 20 hand-milked cows c.1900-1929 [REF AEN, Jansen family].

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 1970-2013
parts.desc: Holstein-type black-pied cows from the modern stalls: the herd grew to about 100 head with young stock, moved to Friesland in 2013 [REF AEN].

parts.name: Cattle in the meadow 2021-2026
parts.desc: A small herd of red-pied MRIJ (Maas-Rijn-IJssel) dual-purpose cows, grass-fed for the farm's cheese [REF OA].

parts.name: Farm horse in the meadow 1325-1960
parts.desc: A draught horse for the hay wagon and the plough on the higher land [REF: 1 horse per farm, houses_1000bc_1600 §S1-S2].

parts.name: Sheep 1175-1900
parts.desc: A few landrace sheep for wool [EST; Rembrandt's 1652 haybarn drawing and Olie's 1893 photograph show sheep in these meadows].

parts.name: Texel sheep today
parts.desc: Texel sheep graze the meadows; their wool goes back on the land as fertiliser [REF OA].

parts.name: Pigs 1175-1850
parts.desc: Two to four long-legged, bristly landrace pigs [REF houses_1000bc_1600: 2-4 pigs per farm; meat bones: beef, then pork].

parts.name: Pigs 1850-1970
parts.desc: Pigs for the household, as most farmers here kept them [REF AEN].

parts.name: Hens 1175-2013
parts.desc: Farmyard hens [EST: generic brown hens; the Barnevelder breed dates from c.1900].

parts.name: Landvarken pigs today
parts.desc: Nederlands Landvarken, a heritage breed, kept outdoors with wallows and fed on garden, dairy, restaurant and bread residues [REF OA].

parts.name: Barnevelder hens today
parts.desc: Barnevelders: chestnut hens with dark double-laced feathers, free-ranging in the sheep stall and the yard; 150-200 brown eggs a year each [REF OA].

parts.name: Geese by the ditch 1175-1600
parts.desc: Geese grazing on the ditch bank. In 1308 Duivendrecht owed the count a tenth of its crops and 8 geese: its first written mention [REF].

parts.name: Towing horse (trekpaard)
parts.desc: The trekschuit's horse walking the west-bank towpath, pulling the 70 m line from a swingletree behind its collar. Usually a boy rode it; it is shown riderless (no people in this model). The horse kept about 7 km/h and was changed at the inns along the route [REF machines_boats §3].

events.title: The first ditch
events.text: Colonists of the Bishop of Utrecht dig drainage ditches at right angles to the Amstel, cutting the bog into cope plots about 113 m wide; farms will stand on mounds at the head of each plot (Duivendrecht PDF §2.2). The drained peat begins to shrink.

events.title: The first farm on the mound
events.text: Colonists build a 17.5 m byre-dwelling on a house mound of peat sods and ditch spoil at the head of the newly drained plot; 'the oldest known occupation between Diemen and Ouderkerk dates from the end of the twelfth century' (Gawronski 2017).

events.title: A longhouse on the old terp
events.text: The peat has sunk too far for grain; the farm turns to cattle. A 22 m longhouse on oak frames and brick pads replaces the first farm (Bos 1984; Bieleman).

events.title: The chimney arrives
events.text: About 1550 the open hearth gives way to a brick fire wall with a smoke hood and a brick stack through the ridge (agriwiki Schouw); leaded glass appears in the windows.

events.title: The storm of 1 August 1674
events.text: A tornado-like storm sweeps Holland and topples the spire of the Ouderkerk church (188°, 2.1 km), leaving a stump until the Amstelkerk of 1775. Thatch and barrack kaps across the polder are torn.

events.title: A new mill for the polder
events.text: The farm's drainage mill Strandvliet (511 m NE) is rebuilt as an octagonal grondzeiler (mill fork).

events.title: Diking charter and the first mill
events.text: On 22 January 1637 the Groot-Duivendrechtse polder receives its diking charter; a wipmolen with a scoop wheel starts pumping the polder from this spot (some sources suggest a mill here already in the late 16th century).

events.title: Strandvliet: the octagonal mill
events.text: The wipmolen is replaced by an octagonal thatched scoop-wheel mill (achtkante grondzeiler) on a brick base.

events.title: Iron stocks
events.text: In 1882/83 the mill gets riveted iron stocks made by Pot; the vlucht is 23.15 m.

events.title: The Archimedean screw
events.text: W. Kool of Moordrecht replaces the scoop wheel by an Archimedean screw for f 10,800, so the mill can lift water higher from the sinking polder. Millwright A.J. Hazenbosch (56) fell to his death during the work on 24 July 1893.

events.title: The mill burns
events.text: On 31 December 1921 Strandvliet catches fire, reportedly because it had run too hard that day. Only the brick base survives.

events.title: The first Dutch youth hostel
events.text: J.H. van Twisk, owner since 1927, opens 'Weideheuvel' in the mill stump: the first youth hostel in the Netherlands.

events.title: The storm of 1 August 1674
events.text: Lightning and a violent storm topple the needle spire of Ouderkerk's church (the same storm wrecked the nave of Utrecht cathedral). The ruin stands for a century.

events.title: The Amstelkerk
events.text: J.E. de Witte's neoclassical Amstelkerk replaces the ruined church: low, white, with a small lantern on the crossing.

events.title: The railway
events.text: 18 December 1843: the Amsterdam-Utrecht railway opens 2.2 km east; steam smoke on the eastern horizon.

events.title: Cuypers' Urbanus spire
events.text: The neo-Gothic Sint-Urbanuskerk rises in Ouderkerk: a 51 m spire on the southern horizon.

events.title: Catenary on the railway
events.text: The Amsterdam-Utrecht line is electrified (1.5 kV DC); steam fades out by 1958.

events.title: The A2 motorway
events.text: 21 Oct 1952 the first carriageway of the A2 opens 810 m north-east; the dual carriageway follows on 1 April 1954.

events.title: The Bijlmermeer
events.text: 1966-1975: 13,000 flats in honeycomb slabs rise 3-4 km east-south-east.

events.title: The ArenA
events.text: The Amsterdam ArenA (now Johan Cruijff ArenA) opens due east, 2.4 km away.

events.title: Trekschuit service Amsterdam–Ouderkerk
events.text: From 1599 a horse-drawn trekschuit ran between Amsterdam and Ouderkerk (later on to Uithoorn and Gouda), three times a day at about 7 km/h. The horse walked the towpath on the west bank, over 40 rolpalen guiding the 70 m line round the bends.

events.title: First Head of the River Amstel
events.text: The Head of the River Amstel, an 8 km race for eights from Ouderkerk to Amsterdam, is rowed for the first time; it passes the farm every March.

events.title: Electric boat to Over-Amstel
events.text: An electric shuttle boat starts bringing guests along the Amstel to the farm's jetty.

interiors.name: The living room, c. 1200
interiors.text: You stand by the wattle screen to the byre and look west down the house. A peat fire smoulders on a domed clay hearth plate in the middle of the floor; there is no chimney, and the smoke climbs into the soot-black rafters and out through the thatch and the smoke holes at the hips. Straw-filled sleeping platforms line both walls, grey-black kogelpots stand in the embers, and beyond the front-room hearth the Pingsdorf spouted pot and a warp-weighted loom. Based on the excavated Westerblokker and Oud-Diemen farms (two heated rooms, 17.5-21 m byre-houses) [REF; layout EST].

interiors.name: The living room, c. 1450
interiors.text: A fire on a raised slab of clay and brick in the middle of the floor, a cauldron on an iron pothook hanging from a beam, red-glazed grapen in the ashes; the smoke has nowhere to go but up into the black rafters and out through the thatch. A Siegburg jug and wooden bowls on a board on trestles, stools, an oak chest, a bed of straw. Open hearths without chimneys until about 1550 (agriwiki Schouw); objects after the Zuid-Holland depot finds [REF; room EST].

interiors.name: The living room, c. 1560
interiors.text: Now the fire burns against a brick fire wall under a wide smoke hood with a red valance on the mantel beam, the cauldron on a pothook from the trammel, as in Pieter Aertsen's Egg Dance (Amsterdam, 1552). Brass basins shine on the wall, a Raeren jug and a candle stand on the linen-covered trestle table, rush-seated chairs, a spinning wheel; leaded glass in the upper halves of the windows. [REF Aertsen; farm use EST]

interiors.name: Woonkeuken at the hearth, c.1650
interiors.text: The open hearth against the brick fire wall: a peat fire on the hearthstone, a cauldron on the pothook, the soot band flanked by new white-and-blue tiles, pewter and Delft plates on the mantel; curtained bedsteden to the left, daylight from the leaded south window. Sources: RCE hallehuis; Agriwiki Schouw, 9.1; De Hooch and Ostade interiors (reconstruction, EST).

dairy_1450.title: From cow to market, c. 1450

steps.title: Milking in the byre
steps.text: Morning and evening the cows are milked by hand where they stand, heads to the wall in the Friese stal; summer milk from the meadow is carried home in two pails on a wooden yoke. Yields were far below modern levels (Bieleman).

steps.title: Setting the milk
steps.text: In the cool middle house the milk is poured into shallow wooden tubs and pans and left a day for the cream to rise.

steps.title: Churning butter
steps.text: The cream is skimmed into the upright stave churn and worked with the plunger until the butter breaks; the buttermilk is drunk.

steps.title: Cheese vat and press
steps.text: Skimmed milk is curdled with rennet in the vat, the curd packed into moulds and pressed under a weighted lever; the cheeses, with the butter, go by boat to Amsterdam (ferry from 1358).

dairy_1450.text: Holland's peat farms switched to almost pure livestock farming in the 14th c. (Bos 1984); dairy for market grows after 1550 (Bieleman). Tools and room after early §3.3–3.4 [forms EST].

steps.title: Milking in the Hollandse stal
steps.text: Twice a day the maids milk the cows by hand, sitting on a low stool behind each stand; in summer milking happens in the meadow. The cows stand in two rows with their heads to the feed passage.

steps.title: Setting the milk in the cellar
steps.text: The milk is poured into wide shallow earthenware dishes on the cellar benches; in the cool, the cream rises overnight. Barred, unglazed windows are opened at night.

steps.title: Churning butter
steps.text: The skimmed cream is churned in the upright plunger churn (stokkarn) until the butter breaks; the buttermilk feeds the family and the pigs.

steps.title: Curdling and moulding cheese
steps.text: Warm milk with rennet sets in the oak curdling tub (kaaskuip); the curd is cut, drained and packed into wooden moulds (kaasvaten).

steps.title: Pressing
steps.text: The lever press squeezes the whey out of the moulded cheese under a stone weight; the cheeses then ripen on boards, turned daily, in the cellar and the front room.

steps.title: To the boat for Amsterdam
steps.text: Butter casks, cheeses and milk barrels go down to the landing on the Amstel and by boat to the Amsterdam markets, a few hours downstream (Ons Amsterdam; HA Amstel-Land).

rembrandt.text: From the farm's waterside on the dike looking S (188°) toward Ouderkerk: the thatched hallehuis at the left, the Amstel at the right and the church spire on the horizon, as in Rembrandt's Cottage beside a Canal: View of Ouderkerk (c.1641, B228). The plate may show Diemen (Met counterproof title).

wind_cap.label: Wind the cap (kruien): rotate the cap, sails and tail about the mill axis
wind_cap.note: Default cap faces SW (225 deg), into the prevailing wind. Apply each rotating part's own spin first, then this yaw (sail and windshaft axes turn with the cap).

mill_octagon.text: The sails turn the windshaft and brake wheel (49 cogs) at 22-25 rpm. Its cogs drive the 24-stave lantern on the upright shaft, which turns about twice as fast (49/24). Until 1893 a 20-stave lantern at its foot drives the 73-cog pit wheel on the water shaft (x 20/73), so the 5.6 m scoop wheel turns at ~13 rpm and drags polder water up the breast into the voorwaterloop. From 1893 a 30-cog bevel gear drives the 39-cog screw gear and the Archimedean screw turns at ~38 rpm. Gear counts are stand-ins (Loenderveense, Driemond); Strandvliet's own were never recorded. Pivots are site coordinates in the 2026 height frame: add the meadow subsidence offset like the parts themselves.

eras.name: Wild peat
eras.text: Raised bog and fen beside a slow peat river, the Amstel. Nobody lives here: only passers-by fishing and hunting leave a trace (a bronze spearhead of c. 900 BC was found at the Amstel mouth).

eras.name: Reclamation
eras.text: Colonists of the Bishop of Utrecht dig ditches at right angles to the Amstel, cutting the bog into long cope plots about 110 m wide. Drained peat starts to shrink and sink.

eras.name: First farm
eras.text: A 17.5 m byre-dwelling of posts, wattle and reed on a house mound raised every decade. No chimney: smoke escapes through the thatch. Barley, oats and flax on the still-high peat.

eras.name: Longhouse
eras.text: The land has sunk too far for grain: dairy cattle take over. A 22 m longhouse; from c. 1550 a brick fire wall, a smoke hood and a chimney stack.

eras.name: Amstellands hallehuis
eras.text: A 29 m hallehuis with a brick front gable under a half-hipped thatched roof. Cows face a central feed passage; the milk cellar sits under a raised opkamer. Windmills drain the polder from 1637.

eras.name: T-farm
eras.text: The front house widens into a T with a tiled roof; the byre stays thatched. The farm's mill, Strandvliet, is rebuilt as an octagonal grondzeiler in 1722. Railway smoke on the horizon from 1843.

eras.name: The 1894 voorhuis
eras.text: A new stal (by 1889), then the wide voorhuis of 1894 with 'Over-Amstel' on its cornice and painted ceilings inside. The mill gets an Archimedean screw in 1893.

eras.name: Working farm
eras.text: The mill burns on 31 Dec 1921; electric pumps take over. Milk churns, a milking machine, the A2 motorway (1952-54), the Bijlmer and the ArenA on the horizon. The herd grows to about 100 head.

eras.name: Disuse
eras.text: The herd moves to Friesland in 2013. The stal roof is patched with tarpaulins weighted by bricks.

eras.name: Over-Amstel today
eras.text: Restored: slate roof, a new white dormer, a restaurant in the old stal, eight new buildings of reclaimed brick, a kitchen garden with a moated labyrinth, and an electric boat to the jetty.
